title: Tiered account routing and ICP fit - QBR & renewal prioritization blueprint
content:
Purpose:
This is a working blueprint for converting raw account signals into an operational routing + priority score used to drive QBR invites, renewal outreach, and dedicated CSM assignment. Unlike the existing segmentation matrices, this doc focuses on combining ICP-fit with deployment topology (hosted/dedicated/private) and regional constraints to produce a single "priority band" and recommended playbook per band.

How to use this sheet (high level):
1) Ingest account-level inputs (ARR, contract_end, deployment_mode, region, usage health metrics, security profile, support trends, product adoption).
2) Compute per-dimension scores (0-10 integer) using rubrics below.
3) Apply weights (tunable) and sum to generate Priority Score (0-100).
4) Map score to Priority Band (Critical / High / Medium / Low).
5) Route to appropriate CSM queue and follow playbook (QBR cadence, renewal owner, exec sponsor outreach).

Scoring rubrics (examples):
- ICP Fit (0-10): product-market alignment. 0 = not target ICP (e.g., consumer app with no AI use), 5 = some fit (ML-enabled product, low token volume), 10 = ideal ICP (AI-native product, high token volume, growth-stage). 
- Deployment Risk (0-10): 0 = hosted (low sales friction), 5 = dedicated (some infra obligations), 10 = private/on-prem or VPC with compliance (high operational risk & revenue significance).
- Region Priority (0-10): weighted by our GTM focus and upcoming renewals. NA = 8, EU = 7, APAC = 5 (default). Adjust for strategic accounts.
- ARR Bucket Score (0-10): <25k=1, 25-100k=4, 100-500k=7, >500k=10.
- Usage Health (0-10): token growth trend, daily active routes, error rate. 0=dead, 5=steady, 10=strong growth + high utilization.
- Support & Incident Trend (0-10): increasing incidents/priority tickets raise score (0 = stable/no high-sev, 10 = repeated P1s last 90 days).
- Feature Adoption (0-10): critical product features used (e.g., streaming, function-calls, custom routing). More adoption -> higher score (indicates deeper integration).

Default weights (tunable in sheet):
- ICP Fit: 18%
- Deployment Risk: 18%
- ARR: 20%
- Usage Health: 16%
- Support Trend: 12%
- Feature Adoption: 8%
- Region Priority: 8%

Priority Score calculation (normalized to 100):
Priority = round( (ICP*0.18 + Deploy*0.18 + ARR*0.20 + Usage*0.16 + Support*0.12 + Feature*0.08 + Region*0.08) * 10 )

Priority Band mapping (example thresholds):
- Critical: 85-100 -> Route to Strategic CSM + AM; schedule Exec QBR within 2 weeks; renewal owner handoff with Sales; create 90-day top risk mitigation plan.
- High: 65-84 -> Dedicated CSM review; QBR within 30 days; consider dedicated enablement workshop; pre-contract renewal health check.
- Medium: 40-64 -> Large field CSM pool; QBR offered quarterly; automated playbooks + templated outreach; monitor for signals.
- Low: 0-39 -> Self-serve / low-touch; annual QBR optional; renewal via standard renewal ops.

Routing rules (examples):
- If Deployment Risk >= 8 AND ARR >= 7 -> Escalate to "dedicated infra" routing lane (SRE + Solutions Eng pre-QBR).
- If Support Trend >= 7 AND Usage Health <= 4 -> Trigger technical triage before QBR; include engineering reviewer.
- If ICP Fit >= 9 AND Priority >= 70 -> Flag for executive sponsor outreach; consider upsell motion.

Renewal cadence & playbook snippets by band:
- Critical:
  - Ownership: Named Strategic CSM + AM + Solutions ENG.
  - Cadence: Monthly outreach; formal QBR 30/60/90 plan; renewal negotiation begins 120 days before EoC.
  - Actions: Renewals kickoff call w/ execs, infra runbook review, SLA & entitlements checklist, custom pricing/commit tiering, plan for Dedicated/Private migration if requested.

- High:
  - Ownership: Named CSM (mid-market) + Sales rep.
  - Cadence: QBR every quarter; renewal outreach begins 90 days prior.
  - Actions: Health review, usage recommendations (batching/quantization), ROI case study, targeted enablement session, check security/compliance gaps.

- Medium:
  - Ownership: Regional CSM pool.
  - Cadence: QBR semi-annual/quarterly offered; renewal ops triggered 60 days prior.
  - Actions: Template-based ROI summary, usage nudges, product tips, monitor for ARR growth triggers.

- Low:
  - Ownership: Growth CS automated flows.
  - Cadence: Annual QBR optional; renewal handled by renewals ops.
  - Actions: Self-serve resources, escalation pathway if signals change.

Sample edge-cases & tie-breakers:
- Ties: If two accounts have identical Priority Score, break ties by ARR then by time-to-contract-end (closer deadlines first).
- Strategic exceptions: Sales or CS manager can manually bump score +10 for named strategic accounts; such overrides must include rationale and owner.

Suggested sheet columns (spreadsheet blueprint):
Account | ARR | Contract_end | ICP_fit (0-10) | Deployment_mode | Deploy_score | Region | Region_score | Usage_health | Support_trend | Feature_adoption | Raw_priority_score | Priority_band | Assigned_owner | Next_QBR_date | Renewal_owner | Notes

Operational checklist before a QBR for high/critical accounts:
- Verify infra architecture diagram + SSO/KMS status
- Confirm performance/latency SLOs & recent SLA breaches
- Compile top 3 product asks and technical blockers from the customer
- Run renewal economics worksheet (current vs proposed commits, burst capacity needs)
- Solutions Eng pre-call if deployment risk >7 or migration planned

Open questions / decisions to finalize in product ops meeting:
- Regional weighting: do we prioritize EU parity above NA for renewals in 2025?
- Weighting for security posture: should KMS/HSM integration bump Deployment Risk weight?
- Thresholds for auto-escalation to Solutions Eng vs manual request.

Next steps (action items):
- CS Analytics: prototype the scoring formula in BigQuery and produce top-200 accounts export by 2025-02-20.
- Solutions Eng: draft a one-pager on "pre-QBR infra checklist" for private/dedicated accounts by 2025-02-25.
- CS Leadership: review regional weights & approve default thresholds in next CS ops on 2025-02-28.

Notes to reviewers: This is intentionally prescriptive — we should prototype on the 200 highest ARR accounts for one quarter to validate predictive power against churn and renewal velocity. Expect iterations.
